youtube.title: The Hindenburg Burned in 34 Seconds. Nobody Knows Why the Hydrogen Leaked
youtube.description:
On 6 May 1937 at Lakehurst, New Jersey, the Hindenburg, filled with hydrogen because the US would not export helium, caught fire while landing after a storm. It burned from tail to nose in about 34 seconds. 62 of 97 aboard survived; 36 people died, including one ground crewman. Investigators blamed a static spark igniting leaking hydrogen, but why the hydrogen was leaking has never been explained.
